reviews.comment: Dr. Igumenova is clear about what will be on each quiz, the midterm, and the final, and she only tests material from the homework. Since she doesn't post slides, taking your own notes (or getting notes from a friend) is required. She also points out the formulas you need for the final and focuses more on understanding than memorization.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Horrible and should be banned from teaching. Simply writes equations without explaining. Expects students to be well versed in quantum mechanics and already be physicists. Her attitude is condescending, unhelpful, cruel. Keeps exams at 7am, which is convenient for her but not for students especially international who rely on buses to get to class.

Lectures are boring and lack engagement. The material is presented in a dry, uninteresting way, making it hard to follow. Unhelpful when it comes to questions or clarification. Grading is inconsistent. Shows no real care for students in the class.

This was one of the most frustrating courses I've taken. Lectures were consistently unclear, and the professor often seemed unprepared. Key concepts were either rushed or skipped, making it extremely hard to follow the material. There was an obvious lack of care for students learning any material and communication with the professor was difficult.

I dont know why Professor Igumenova gets such a bad rep. I thought she was really good. She is a little hard to understand at times but she respects her students and will slow down in lectures if needed and allows questions to be asked for clarification. The class as a whole is just difficult.

She gets a really bad reputation; compared to the other professor, she is a saint. Multiple choice exams & quizzes, if you pay attention & take notes in class, you should pass easily. What she says is on the exam is accurate. Copy & paste questions from notes. She can go really, really fast, but if you ask a question, she will slow down & explain.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lowkey not bad. Class is hard and she only grades by quizzes and tests. However, the tests and quizzes are fair. She only puts what is on the notes on the exam and quiz. The SI and TA help A LOT. Study, and you will be fine. Notes are fill-in-the-blank, though, so make a friend or go to class lol.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wanna take one of the worst classes offered by tamu? Try getting spitroasted by tim reaper and his brain dead lackey. Expect no SI, misleading exam review guides, and pretty much no support from either instructor. "Just know general topics not specifics" haha ok. Be prepared to analyze every microcosm of each slide to even get a chance at passing.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 1st 2 quizzes get prepared to read. I forgot to the 1st time & procrastination got me the 2nd time so i had only read 1/2 of it & the grade was horrible. I got 100s for the remaining quizzes & still couldnt manage an A. Be sure to research well for the group project, if your project is well done she will ask questions unrelated to your presentation
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You lose 1 point per unexcused absence. The grade makeup is 6 quizzes worth 9 points each, and the rough draft and final project makeup the remaining 36 points. If you do the reading ahead of class and pay attention during lecture, you should be prepared for the quiz at the end of class. Project's not that hard just be sure to know the topic well
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She mostly reads the slides and does not really explain much. No study guides and test heavy. She often said phrases such as "Just know general not specifics' or "This will not be on the exam". BEWARE: IT WILL BE ON THE EXAM AND SPECIFIC. I would never take a class with this professor again. If you ever want to feel cheated on exams, take her.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Igumenova's class was difficult since the grades were dependent on the quizzes which weren't based on things we learned, but articles assigned for HW (based on reading comprehension). The final group project was okay, she asked some groups very hard questions. She did curve our grade in the end (got an A for 88). NOT AN EASY INTRODUCTORY CLASS.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her grading is pretty stern. There's only 6 quizzes, and each point you lose is a point off your overall grade, so you can barely miss questions. Group project isn't bad if you get a good group, but she asks hard questions at the end for no reason. Very strict for it being 1 credit hour, and got annoyed at the class frequently for little things.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Would not take again. Had friends in other classes that had the same class, diff. prof., and got an easy A. The margin of error in this class is so small that if you miss 4 quiz questions (6 quizzes, 3-4 questions each) you can't get an A. Group project seems easy but after you present she humiliates your group, goes way to fast through slides
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Igumenova has a slight accent & will lecture about test materials after the test. Most test (which are once a week) are 3-4 questions max! One group project & 6 quizzes are the only grades so pray you get a good group. She struggles to understand the baseline knowledge of many students expecting them to know far to much for a intro course.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Unforgiving & Critical Grading, Monotonous, 1 Group Project, 3-4 Question Quizzes Over 1 Book & Many Articles, Irrelevant & Fast Lecturing, Not An Easy (A) Class, Cannot Procrastinate Work

Grade Breakdown: 6 Quizzes - ~9 Points Each, 1 Group Project Draft - 16 Points, And Final Presentation - 30 Points. (-1 Points for Every Absence)

reviews.comment: Grades come from not a lot of quizzes based on short readings. They're not too hard but you can't afford to get it wrong because it will tank your grade. She has lectures that are interesting but are not needed to learn for anything. Final is a group project.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has an unforgiving grading system, 6 quizzes, one for almost every week of the first half of the semester. These quizzes are based on assigned reading that is in canvas. If you miss 4 questions throughout the entire semester you will not get an A in the class, since each question on the 6 individual quizzes are worth 3 points.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Igumenova was a clear lecturerer, and frequently related her class to real world concepts and topics. The final project was a group assignment, done over the semester, and wasn't hard. The professor wasn't particularly warm to the students, but was understanding and VERY lenient with my group. Not too much hw, but assigned reading is essential.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Igumenova was very knowledgable about the topics discussed and encouraged class discussions which were very constructive. The group project was the most challenging aspect of the course, as well as the readings required.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are very interesting. The assignments may take a bit of time, but they are very doable. Reading the assigned material is a must. The main thing to be aware of is the group project. You will need to come prepared, but so long as you do, she is a very fair grader.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You are graded by a few quizzes and a group project but actually read the articles she assigns and you should be fine. She is a knowledgeable and meticulous professor. She harshly critiqued groups in front of the class after their presentations. She has very high expectations of what you should know even if it is beyond the class material.

reviews.comment: Alright prof. Her grading system is stressful and you will have to do a group project.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very few grades. Class doesn't take up the majority of your time, but you have like 4 quizzes, 2 reading essays and 1 final group project. The readings take a while, and you have to be CAUTIOUS with not loosing points in your readings/quizzes. Not sure how other classes work and if they are similar, but I HATE how they are few grades. Dont Recommen

reviews.comment: Although our class was over Zoom, I loved Professor Igumenova's lectures. They were intriguing (especially the lectures concerning mRNA vaccines). We read The Double Helix by James Watson and answered questions as well. There were many quizzes and a group project, which were all manageable considering her amazing feedback. Would recommend!

reviews.comment: There were very few grades over the course of the semester, almost half of your grade was comprised of four question quizzes that covered 3-4 readings each. Students can be at fault for things, but she is also very unaccommodating given the circumstances of our semester. For an introductory course, some topics were very advanced and challenging.
